newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS IOC REP ACQUITAL.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS IOC REP ACQUITAL.

text.p: Bulgaria's Supreme Court of Appeals overturned a lower court's ruling to free Ivan Slavkov, the representative to the International Olympic Committee (IOC) from charges of illegal ownership of weapons, state radio said.

"The court found that it lacks evidence of Slavkov's intention to turn in the illegally held weapons and munition. The way they were stored and displayed at his home showed a sense of being above reproach," the radio said quoting a court official.

Slavkov, who is a son-in-law of Bulgaria's ousted communist dictator Todor Zhivkov, went on trial in March last year for alleged embezzlement of several thousand dollars and illegal ownership of two pistols, six rifles and 200 cartridges.

The supreme court accepted a second ruling of the Sofia City court, which acquited Slavkov from the misappropriation charges, after establishing that he had returned in 1989 the funds to the Bulgarian Olympic Committe which he chairs.
Slavkov has been under investigation since 1990 when he was briefly arrested for illegal ownership of weapons, which were exhibited on the walls of his house as gifts from foreigners.
He was banned from travelling abroad as an IOC member and barred from attending the Olympic Games in Barcelona in 1992 and in Lillehamer in 1994 because of the charges.
Slavkov's son Todor, is on bail awaiting a rape trial.

His father-in-law, who ruled Bulgaria for 35 years, was acquitted last year after appealing against a seven-year jail sentence for embezzling state funds, but remains under house arrest on separate charges.
